goal: Decide whether one text message is likely a scam, likely safe, or uncertain, and explain why in plain words an older adult can understand.

message.text: MEDICARE ALERT: Your benefits will be suspended today. To keep your coverage, buy a $200 gift card and send the card number at medicare-help.co/renew

explanation: This looks like a scam. The message asks for a gift card, which is a strong warning sign. It also has a link that looks like the real Medicare website, which is another strong warning sign. Government agencies never ask for gift cards, and this message is trying to trick you into giving money.
what_to_do: Do not reply, do not tap any link, and do not send money or codes. If you are worried, call Medicare at 1-800-555-0101 (from our trusted list).
guide_tip: Tip from our guide (G01): Do not buy the card. Hang up or delete the text and call the agency using the number on your card or letter.
